headline: Sterling touched a three-month low near 1.3190 against the dollar at about 14:05 Dubai on Thursday, after oil climbed back above $100 (about £76) on Chinese fuel export curbs and the US 10-year yield reached its highest since 2002. It has since recovered to about 1.3224, and US jobless claims at 197,000, slightly fewer than expected, moved it very little.

happened.result: 197,000 new claims in the week to 26 September, against about 201,000 expected and down 1,000 on the week before, the lowest since July. Continuing claims fell to 1.701 million, a three-year low, and the Challenger survey showed planned layoffs in September down 18% on August.
happened.why: Fewer people losing their jobs points to a strong US labour market, which normally keeps a Fed rise in play and supports the dollar; this time the dollar index touched about 102, but sterling had already fallen a long way and barely reacted.
happened.effect: GBP/USD edged up from 1.3228 just before the release to about 1.3235 within two minutes and held near there until about 16:45 Dubai, then eased back to about 1.3222 by 17:20 Dubai.

happened.event: Oil jumps back above $100 on Chinese fuel export curbs, with US yields at 24-year highs
happened.result: Reuters reported that Chinese refiners had suspended October fuel exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau, and that PetroChina had cancelled some petrol and jet fuel cargoes. Oil reversed its morning fall: by 09:23 UTC (13:23 Dubai) Brent for December was up 2.4% at $100.36 (about £75.89) and US crude up 2.5% at $92.70 (about £70.10). The US 10-year yield rose to about 5.33%, its highest since 2002, and FXStreet described the UK factory survey published this morning as soft.
happened.why: Dearer oil adds to inflation worries, pushes US yields higher and sours the market mood, all of which draws money into the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3222 at 12:35 Dubai to 1.3206 by 13:00 Dubai, steadied, then dropped to a three-month low near 1.3190 at about 14:05 Dubai. It recovered to about 1.3243 by 15:55 Dubai without a named piece of news, and was near 1.3224 at 17:35 Dubai.

happened.event: Bank of England Governor Bailey opens the Future of Money conference
happened.result: Bailey gave opening remarks at a conference on digital money held in honour of the economist Charles Goodhart. The morning briefings read carried his warning that the AI boom could trigger market shocks, and nothing on the path of Bank Rate.
happened.why: Only remarks pointing to higher or lower UK interest rates tend to move the pound much, so a speech without them leaves sterling to follow the dollar.
happened.effect: GBP/USD was about 1.3232 just before he spoke and moved between 1.3227 and 1.3236 in the first five minutes. It then drifted down to about 1.3219 by 08:38 UTC (12:38 Dubai) as the dollar stayed firm.

happened.event: Dollar buying at the London open
happened.result: As European trading began, the dollar rose broadly. Reuters reported the dollar index up 0.38% at 101.58, the euro down 0.3% at $1.1299, its first fall below $1.13 since May 2025, and US 10-year and 30-year yields at new highs of about 5.34% and 5.67% overnight, after their largest quarterly rise since 1994. None of the sources read names a single piece of news behind the move at the open.
happened.why: Higher US yields make dollars more rewarding to hold, so money moves into the dollar and each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3263 at 11:10 Dubai to a low near 1.3226 at 11:45 Dubai, a drop of about 0.28% in 35 minutes, then steadied near 1.3235.

happened.event: Sterling drifts lower in Asian trading
happened.result: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3271 at 05:10 Dubai to about 1.3252 by 07:40 Dubai. The dollar also firmed against the yen after Japan's business survey, and none of the sources read names a single piece of news behind the move.
happened.why: When the dollar is broadly firmer in thin overnight trading, each pound buys fewer dollars and so fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: A fall of about 0.15% over two and a half hours, taking GBP/AED from about 4.874 to about 4.867.

happened.result: Big manufacturers' confidence came in at +24 against +25 expected, and big service firms at +35 against +36. Bank of Japan meeting notes showed some members open to faster rises, but traders trimmed bets on a rise in October and the dollar rose to about 157.87 yen.
happened.why: A firmer dollar against the yen usually comes with a firmer dollar more generally, which means fewer dirhams per pound.
happened.effect: GBP/USD barely moved at the release, easing from 1.3265 to 1.3262 within five minutes.

happened.event: Fed's Kashkari speaks in New York
happened.result: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said inflation of about 3% is still too high and the latest data do not change his view. He has pencilled in one more rise this year and another in 2027, and said the longer the economy stays strong, the more he questions whether policy is tight at all.
happened.why: A Fed official leaning towards more rises supports US yields and the dollar, so each pound buys fewer dirhams.
happened.effect: GBP/USD dipped from 1.3263 to 1.3260 at the start of his remarks, in thin trading at the daily rollover, then recovered to about 1.3265 within ten minutes.

drivers.title: US bond yields
drivers.text: The US 10-year yield rose to about 5.33% on Thursday, its highest since 2002, and the 30-year to about 5.67%, after their largest quarterly rise since 1994. High US yields keep the dollar attractive to hold and remain the main weight on sterling.

drivers.title: Fed rate expectations
drivers.text: After Wednesday's cooler inflation figures, markets put about a 39% chance on a quarter-point Fed rise at the 28 October meeting, and the CME FedWatch tool shows about an 87% chance of a rise by the end of the year. Thursday's jobless claims, at 197,000, show a labour market still tight, and Fed speakers lean firm. Friday's jobs report is the next big test.

drivers.title: A broadly stronger dollar
drivers.text: The dollar index touched about 102 on Thursday afternoon, its highest since April 2025, after a sixth quarterly gain in a row. The euro is below $1.13, so sterling's fall today is part of a wider dollar move rather than news particular to the UK.

drivers.title: Oil and the Middle East
drivers.text: Brent rose back above $100 (about £76) on Thursday morning, up about 2.4%, after reports that Chinese refiners had halted October fuel exports. Gulf crude flows are close to pre-war levels, but fuel stocks are very low and US-Iran talks have stalled, so oil remains sensitive to news from the Gulf and from China.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 17 September, with three of the nine members voting for a rise, and markets price a quarter-point rise at the 5 November meeting. On 29 September Alan Taylor, one of the six who voted to hold, said the case for a rise was not compelling unless high energy prices fed into broader inflation. At about 1.3224, GBP/AED is near 4.857 at the peg of 3.6725, just above Thursday's three-month low near 1.3190.

lower: The US factory survey (ISM) this afternoon above the 54.8 forecast, which would point to a strong US economy and support the dollar.
US jobs figures on Friday stronger than the 89K forecast, or wages rising faster than 0.3%, which would revive the chance of an October Fed rise and strengthen the dollar.
US 10-year yields rising further from their highest since 2002, which would keep drawing money into the dollar.
Oil climbing further on Chinese export curbs or renewed escalation with Iran, which tends to strengthen the dollar.
higher: The US factory survey this afternoon below 54.8, which would make an October Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Fed's Waller this afternoon sounding patient about further rises, which would lower US yields and weaken the dollar.
US jobs figures on Friday weaker than the 89K forecast, or unemployment above 4.1%, which would make an October Fed rise less likely and weaken the dollar.
Oil falling back below $100 or progress in the talks with Iran, which reduces the demand for dollars.
watch: The US factory survey (ISM) and a speech by the Fed's Waller, both at 18:00 Dubai today, with 54.8 forecast for the survey; a lower reading or a patient tone would help someone selling pounds for dirhams. Friday's US jobs report at 16:30 Dubai, with 89K jobs, 4.1% unemployment and 0.3% wage growth forecast, is the week's main event: weaker figures would help, stronger would hurt.
